```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's channel suits a solo, agent-run company aiming for a paying customer in 90 days. The Shopify App Store is a self-serve marketplace with built-in merchant discovery, and the brief backs its ads channel with a sourced ~$6 CPC figure. B's best-sourced channel is SEO content, cited at $480–942 CAC. That is a generic B2B SaaS statistic, not specific to prerendering, and against a $29–49/mo entry price it implies a payback far longer than 90 days. B's community channel is explicitly [unsourced].",
    "B faces a sourced structural headwind that A lacks. Google's own documentation calls dynamic rendering a 'workaround, not a long-term solution' and points developers to SSR/SSG frameworks, so B's addressable market is shrinking. A's market is saturated but not contracting.",
    "A's demand evidence is better linked. Its merchant pain quote has a specific thread URL showing a failed manual workaround, and the brief cites a sourced solo-founder case (Zigpoll, $125K MRR) for the same problem and model. B's Reddit quotes are identified only by subreddit and year, with no URLs, and its one named testimonial comes from a vendor's own pricing page.",
    "A's competitor pricing is fully itemized with URLs for six apps. B's brief says 'see competitors list for full pricing' but supplies no such list, so most of its competitive picture cannot be checked.",
    "B's cloaking-policy risk adds an ongoing support burden that the brief itself calls unusual for a one-person operation. A's main compliance burden is a one-time DPA/privacy review, which is more tractable."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence. The two Reddit quotes have no thread URLs, only a subreddit and year, so they cannot be verified and count as effectively unsourced. The only attributed quote is a vendor testimonial on Prerender.io's own pricing page, which is self-interested marketing rather than independent demand. A close second is the $480–942 SEO CAC figure, which is generic B2B SaaS data presented as 'externally validated' for this category.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Both ideas are saturated categories with free or cheap incumbents, and neither brief shows a new entrant landing a paying customer within 90 days. A's own brief notes the category leader took two years to reach traction and that zero-review apps face trust barriers. A wins mainly because B carries a sourced platform-level headwind (Google deprecating the technique), thinner and unlinked demand evidence, and worse channel economics for the 90-day window, not because A's path to a first paying customer is well evidenced."
}
```
